overhead.method: An open-loop load generator in the benchmark process sends each scenario to the mock provider directly and through the gateway (each in its own process, loopback). The mock answers after a fixed 100 ms time to first token and streams 500 tokens at 2000 tokens/s. Each stream is one keep-alive connection, opened before the run, with its own schedule of evenly spaced send times (5 requests/s non-streaming, 1.25 requests/s streaming) starting at a seeded random phase, so connections do not fire together; a request still running at the next scheduled time delays the next one, and client-side latency always counts from the scheduled time (coordinated omission included). Added TTFB is the gateway's own per-request measure from its traces (`addedTtfbMs`: from the start of request handling to forwarding upstream, with a sub-millisecond clock in the benchmark), so it is paired per request; it does not include time a request waits before the gateway starts handling it, nor the response path. The client-side columns are absolute percentiles of each path, never subtracted from each other; "outside the provider" is each request's TTFB minus the mock's own wait for that request (the `x-mock-wait-ms` header), paired per request, so the mock's timer jitter drops out. An added TTFB SLO row is met only when both the gateway-measured value and the client-side TTFB outside the provider through the gateway (an upper bound on what the gateway adds, which includes queueing before handling) are under target. n is the number of samples behind each percentile. CPU is the gateway process's user plus system time over the run's wall time (100% is one core); RSS growth is its peak during the run above its size just before it; per 100 streams is the slope between 100 and 500 streams. The gateway runs examples/policy with every budget level enforced at a limit the load never reaches, no rate limits, guardrails on, traces written and metrics kept.

headroom.note: session-aware reserves the same as worst-case here: the estimator is not given the session's previous cache read share yet (src/policy/decide.ts passes none), and the route sets no reserveOutputTokens.

cache.note: The naive proxy flattens `system` into a string, which drops the cache breakpoint on the system block. This session also marks the newest user block, and that breakpoint caches the whole prefix, the flattened system text included, so through the naive proxy the session still reads almost the same prefix from cache and costs about the same; its usage still differs from the direct run (conformance test C15b fails on it).
